newsitem.title: MOZAMBIQUE: Mozambique wins $100 million World Bank credit.
newsitem.headline: Mozambique wins $100 million World Bank credit.

text.p: Negotiations between the World Bank and the Mozambican government ended on Friday with agreement on $100 million credit for Mozambique, the central bank in Maputo announced on Friday.
In a communique, Banco de Mozambique said the credit was to be repaid over 40 years, including a 10-year grace period.
The money will be used to finance imports as part of a structural adjustment programme which began in 1987.
Michel Camdessus, managing director of the International Monetary Fund (IMF), visiting Mozambique two months ago, pledged support for a reduction of Mozambique's $5.5 billion foreign debt.
He said that the IMF and the World Bank would "agree to make loans or grants in order to reduce what is owed to us to a sustainable level, provided all other creditors take a similar initiative".
Camdessus said he was impressed by the Mozambique government's achievements and that evidence showed structural adjustment was working.
"Growth is there, at a continuously high level, exports are increasing at an impressive rate, the currency is very stable and the latest news on inflation is encouraging," he said at the time.

The Paris Club of creditor nations last month agreed to restructure Mozambique's debt and, in a departure from tradition, signalled a willingness to hold further talks if the debt relief was not enough.

Mozambique is one of the world's poorest countries following a protracted guerilla war against Portuguese colonialists, which led to independence in 1975, followed by civil war which lasted until 1992.
